reason: E1 directly supports the stability of the bcc phase and the robust Tc up to 190.6 GPa, but neither E1 nor E2 provides evidence for the mechanistic claims about preserved electron–phonon coupling, density of states, or the causal role of configurational entropy in lattice stabilization. E2 concerns a different material system (metal telluride) and only loosely supports the general idea of entropy enhancing robustness, not the specific bcc mechanism.
premises: The bcc lattice in (TaNb)0.67(HfZrTi)0.33 is stable up to 190.6 GPa without a structural phase transition.
The superconducting Tc of this HEA is nearly invariant under pressure up to 190.6 GPa.
The robust superconductivity is due to preserved electron–phonon coupling and density of states in the stable bcc lattice.
